chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah narrated it from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Isma'il ibn Mirrar, from Yunus ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from 'Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:
Whoever comes to an estate, then does not intend to stay for ten days, he shortens the salat (prayer). But if he intends to stay for ten days, he performs the salat (prayer) in full.

key_terms.أَتَمَّ: he performed the salat (prayer) in full
key_terms.ضَيْعَةً: an estate, property, or cultivated land belonging to a person
key_terms.عَشَرَةَ أَيَّامٍ: the ten-day period that determines the ruling of travel prayer
key_terms.قَصَّرَ: he shortened the salat (prayer), meaning qasr
key_terms.ٱلْمُقَامَ: staying or residing in a place

ai.seo_question: When does a traveler pray qasr or full salat (prayer) upon arriving at his estate?
ai.summary: This hadith states the legal ruling for a traveler who comes to his estate or property. If he does not intend to remain for ten days, he offers shortened salat (prayer); if he intends a stay of ten days, he performs the salat (prayer) in full.
